name: Primary Acquired Red Cell Aplasia
aliases: Primary Acquired Pure Red Cell Aplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Primary Acquired Red Cell Aplasia

criteria.description: Severe normocytic normochromic anemia with reticulocytopenia
Marked reduction or absence of erythroid precursors in bone marrow with normal myeloid and megakaryocytic lineages
Exclusion of secondary causes such as thymoma, autoimmune disorders, infections, or drug-induced aplasia
No evidence of hemolysis or bleeding to explain anemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of severe anemia with reticulocytopenia, bone marrow showing erythroid aplasia, and exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of secondary etiologies and confirmation by bone marrow biopsy.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe normocytic normochromic anemia with reticulocytopenia
searchTerms: marked anemia with few young red cells
normocytic anemia with low retic count

pathognomonic.symptomName: Marked erythroid hypoplasia in bone marrow
searchTerms: very low red blood cell production
bone marrow not making red cells

common.symptomName: Dyspnea on exertion secondary to anemia
Fatigue related to decreased oxygen carrying capacity
searchTerms: weakness related to poor oxygen delivery

common.symptomName: Tachycardia as compensatory response to anemia
searchTerms: increased heart rate compensating for low blood
tachycardia from low red cell count

occasional.symptomName: Mild jaundice due to ineffective erythropoiesis
searchTerms: jaundice due to poor red cell production
head pain due to low blood oxygen

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms secondary to severe anemia (e.g., dizziness, syncope)
searchTerms: neurological symptoms due to severe anemia
lightheadedness related to low red cells
autoimmune symptoms like rash and arthritis
immune system causing skin and joint problems

laboratory: Severe anemia with low reticulocyte count
Bone marrow biopsy showing erythroid aplasia
Absence of hemolysis markers (normal LDH, bilirubin)
imaging: Chest imaging to exclude thymoma or mediastinal masses
genetic: No known consistent genetic mutations; idiopathic in most cases
other: Exclusion of secondary causes including infections, drugs, and autoimmune diseases

distinguishingFeatures: Bone marrow hypocellularity involving all lineages
Identifiable secondary cause such as thymoma, parvovirus B19 infection, or drug exposure
Dysplastic changes in bone marrow cells

redFlags: Rapidly worsening anemia with severe reticulocytopenia
Presence of pancytopenia suggesting progression to aplastic anemia
Evidence of thymoma or other malignancy on imaging
references: Young NS. Acquired aplastic anemia. Ann Intern Med. 2002;136(7):534-46.
